questions.q: What is LTV Global Industries, as this capstone defines it?
options: A fictional multinational manufacturer and distributor of industrial equipment and parts, used as the single scenario for this entire capstone
A real, named Salesforce customer whose actual production org this course reproduces
A Salesforce-internal team that reviews Technical Architect certification candidates
A third-party consulting firm that specializes in Salesforce data migrations
questions.explain: LTV Global Industries is a fictional company built specifically for this capstone, so the whole course can work against one consistent, realistic scenario instead of disconnected examples.

questions.q: Which three regions does LTV Global operate in?
options: North America, South America, and Africa
North America, EMEA, and APAC
EMEA only, with no other regions
APAC, Antarctica, and North America
questions.explain: LTV Global operates in North America (headquarters), EMEA (subject to GDPR), and APAC (its newest, fastest-growing region).

questions.q: Why does this lesson say LTV Global's scale turns the project into a Technical Architect-level problem rather than an admin configuration task?
options: Because the company only has a handful of users and records, which always requires an architect
Because of the combination of ~10,000 internal users, millions of customer records, multiple legacy systems, complex security needs, and high-volume integrations
Because Salesforce requires every customer with more than one business unit to hire a Technical Architect by policy
Because the company has no legacy systems at all, making the design unusually simple
questions.explain: It's the combination of scale (users and records), legacy debt, security complexity, and integration volume that makes this an architecture problem rather than a configuration task — any one of those alone might not.

questions.q: Which business unit does this lesson identify as having the highest transaction volume at LTV Global?
options: Equipment Financing
Field Service & Support
Parts & Aftermarket Distribution
Equipment Manufacturing & Sales
questions.explain: Parts & Aftermarket Distribution is called out specifically as the highest-transaction-volume business unit, which matters later for large data volume and integration design.

questions.q: What does this lesson say Chapter 6's Architecture Review Board defense represents for the capstone as a whole?
options: An optional bonus exercise unrelated to the rest of the course
The moment every other chapter's work was building toward — presenting and defending the full design
A separate certification exam administered outside this course
A chapter that replaces the need to complete Chapters 2 through 5
questions.explain: The lesson frames Chapter 6's ARB defense as the culmination the rest of the capstone (requirements, core architecture, integration, delivery strategy, deliverables) is explicitly preparing the student for.
